sunday 13th september 2026
twenty-fourth sunday in ordinary time
how often to forgive
in our gospel this weekend st matthew continues to deal with relations between
christians, focusing on the need for forgiveness. peter asks jesus how often he
should forgive his brother and then answers the question by suggesting seven
just as in days of old as in our own time and the time of jesus christ there was no
limit to hatred, evil and vengeance, likewise in the eyes of jesus there is no limit
to mercy and forgiveness.
the parable of the unforgiving official is told to underline the need for forgiveness.
when the accounts are audited there is a huge deficiency. the sum is deliberately
extravagant to heighten the contrast with the small amount owed to the official.
despite the king cancelling the official’s debt he learns nothing. the official seems
to forget that he has had his debt cancelled. forgetfulness of our own sins and
human weakness can lead us to lack of compassion. through forgetfulness of
god’s compassion, we can end up becoming cruel to each other.
in the first reading we have good advice which underlines the futility of vengeance
and anger. “if a man nurses anger against another, can he demand compassion
from the lord? showing no pity for a man like himself, can he then plead for his
own sins?” nursing anger and not forgiving disables us and renders us defenseless
when we look for forgiveness for our own sins.
remember - “to err is human; to forgive is, divine”. alexander pope
